answer: A concrete Sybil defence in an AI-agent economy is a per-identity work bond: each agent locks stake released only after its operator's identity survives a long resolution window, and duplicates are slashed, burning stake. Creating 500 fakes means locking stake for each and leaving it idle for months. The cost is locked capital plus its opportunity cost, and per-identity yield is capped, so N fakes never out-earn one honest agent. The registry holds one kernel of truth, so defenders dedupe cheaply while every extra inlet for fraud costs a full bond, leaving sable margins for real operators.
